content:
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

DATA ENGINEERING | TEST DATA AUTOMATION

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, and engineering data analysis. Builds Python tools to process test-rig data, check results against specifications, and generate reports. Developed an internal processing tool used by four test engineers and a Power BI dashboard used by around 15 colleagues. Experienced with Python, SQL Server, MATLAB/Simulink and test data; currently completing an online data engineering course.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS), SQL, MATLAB/Simulink, Excel/VBA
Data tools: SQL Server, Power BI, SQLite, Flask
Engineering and testing: ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Development tools: Git (personal projects), Docker Compose (tutorial project)

EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | Setúbal
Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare reports for OEM customers.
- Develop Python scripts to parse TDMS and CSV rig outputs (around 2 GB per week), check channels against test specifications, and generate standard report figures. Reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test.
- Maintain an internal data-processing tool scheduled nightly on a laboratory PC. It writes summary results to a staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database and is used by four other test engineers.
- Query the plant’s test-results database for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Built a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; used by around 15 validation and design engineers.
- Correlate rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that cut warranty returns for the part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive, used to select rig load profiles that match customer duty cycles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps | Porto
Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed centrifugal pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and produced manufacturing drawings with GD&T; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Performed structural FEA of casings in ANSYS. Supported a move from grey cast iron to ductile iron for one casing family, saving 12% in material cost.
- Wrote a LabVIEW data-acquisition program for the pump performance test bench, reducing test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes.
- Supported conversion of the performance test bench to a Siemens S7 PLC-controlled setup, changing setpoints and timers in TIA Portal under the automation engineer’s supervision.

SELECTED DATA PROJECTS

Rig data processing and reporting tool | Corvane Automotive Components | 2021–Present
- Developed Python scripts to parse TDMS and CSV test-rig outputs, flag channels outside test specifications, and generate report figures. Processes around 2 GB of data per week from six rigs.
- Runs nightly on a laboratory PC using Windows Task Scheduler, writes summary results to a staging table in SQL Server, and is used by four other test engineers.
- Technologies: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server.

Test results dashboard | Corvane Automotive Components | 2023
- Built a Power BI dashboard showing pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation, used by around 15 validation and design engineers.
- Technologies: Power BI, SQL.

Bike-sharing Trips API | Personal learning project | 2025
- Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints.
- Followed a tutorial to run the project with Docker Compose; maintains personal project repositories using Git.

EDUCATION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

Online Data Engineering Course | In progress
Completed 6 of 9 modules

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)


COVER LETTER

Dear Halden Pay Data Platform Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. After 12 years in mechanical engineering, testing and validation, I am moving toward data engineering, building on practical experience turning engineering test data into reliable checks, reports and decisions.

At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts that process around 2 GB of TDMS and CSV test-rig output each week, check channels against specifications and generate report figures. This reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test. I also maintain a tool scheduled nightly on a laboratory PC that writes summary results to a SQL Server staging table and is used by four other test engineers. A Power BI dashboard built on that table gives around 15 validation and design colleagues visibility into pass/fail trends and cycles to failure. These projects have taught me to focus on dependable, reusable tools and the needs of the people who rely on their outputs.

My experience to date is with engineering data workflows and internal tools, rather than operating a cloud data platform. I am currently completing an online data engineering course, with six of nine modules completed, and am keen to continue developing in this field. Halden Pay’s focus on shared platform capabilities, collaboration across teams and taking ownership of problems particularly appeals to me. I am also happy to commute to Lisbon for a hybrid role.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my test-data automation experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Best regards,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, concise, professional, and appropriately tailored to Halden Pay’s Data Platform role. It uses credible metrics—2 GB of weekly data, a reduction from three days to half a day, four users, and approximately 15 dashboard users—to demonstrate practical impact. The letter is also commendably honest about the candidate’s current experience being focused on engineering-data workflows rather than cloud platforms. The main weakness is that the final paragraph is somewhat generic and foregrounds missing cloud-platform experience instead of emphasizing transferable evidence such as reusable tooling, data-quality checks, stakeholder collaboration, and ownership.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The cover letter uses ATS-friendly plain text, standard headings, readable paragraphs, and relevant terms including Python, SQL Server, data engineering, data platform, Power BI, test data, and hybrid. Its keyword coverage is necessarily limited because the candidate does not have experience with Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, or cloud data warehouses; these must not be added. The document should perform well for parsing, but AI screening for a senior data-platform role may remain limited because the letter does not explicitly mention data modelling, open-source practices, Git, or Portuguese, all of which are relevant to the advertisement and supported by the candidate’s material.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows strong transferable experience in Python-based data processing, automated data-quality checks, SQL Server workflows, reusable internal tooling, reporting automation, and collaboration with engineering users. It aligns particularly well with the role’s emphasis on reusable frameworks, platform users, ownership, and reducing unnecessary manual work. However, the candidate’s material shows genuine gaps in production data-platform or cloud-warehouse operation at scale, advanced SQL/query optimisation, dimensional data modelling, Google Cloud or comparable cloud technologies, and graph modelling. The letter also does not currently evidence the candidate’s curiosity about open-source practices or mention native Portuguese, despite the candidate material supporting both Git-based personal projects and Portuguese fluency. Good professional English is demonstrated by the quality of the letter, and Portuguese is a stated nice-to-have.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the paragraph beginning "My experience to date is with engineering data workflows," replace the sentence "My experience to date is with engineering data workflows and internal tools, rather than operating a cloud data platform" with a more positive but still accurate formulation such as: "My experience so far has focused on building reusable engineering-data workflows and internal tools, including automated specification checks, SQL Server reporting workflows, and a dashboard used by validation and design teams." This preserves truthfulness without leading with a limitation.

2. In the same paragraph, add one concise sentence showing the supported evidence for curiosity about data architecture and open-source practices: "Alongside my professional work, I am completing an online data engineering course and building small Python projects with Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, and Git." Do not describe these projects as production systems or claim professional cloud experience.

3. In the final paragraph, add Portuguese as a relevant qualification for the Lisbon-based team, using wording such as: "As a native Portuguese speaker with fluent professional English, I would also bring effective communication in the company’s local working context." Only include this if the letter is intended to retain a brief qualifications sentence; do not add unsupported claims about multilingual business experience.

4. In the paragraph describing the Corvane work, consider changing "These projects have taught me to focus on dependable, reusable tools and the needs of the people who rely on their outputs" to "These projects required me to build dependable, reusable tools, define automated checks against specifications, and respond to the needs of the engineers who rely on their outputs." This more directly mirrors the advertisement’s focus on reusable platform capabilities, data quality, and collaboration while remaining supported by the candidate’s experience.

These projects required me to build dependable, reusable tools, define automated checks against specifications, and respond to the needs of the engineers who rely on their outputs.

My experience so far has focused on building reusable engineering-data workflows and internal tools, including automated specification checks, SQL Server reporting workflows, and a dashboard used by validation and design teams. I am currently completing an online data engineering course, with six of nine modules completed, and am keen to continue developing in this field. Alongside my professional work, I am completing an online data engineering course and building small Python projects with Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, and Git. Halden Pay’s focus on shared platform capabilities, collaboration across teams and taking ownership of problems particularly appeals to me. I am also happy to commute to Lisbon for a hybrid role.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my test-data automation experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.

Best regards,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is professional, truthful, and supported by strong quantified evidence: processing approximately 2 GB of data weekly, reducing report preparation from three days to half a day, and supporting four engineers and approximately 15 dashboard users. It clearly explains the transition from mechanical engineering to data engineering without claiming unsupported cloud or platform experience. The main content weakness is repetition: the online data engineering course is mentioned twice in the same paragraph. The letter also remains somewhat generic about how the candidate's experience relates to Halden Pay's values and reusable platform work. Its candid positioning is appropriate, but the evidence supports an emerging or transitioning data engineer more strongly than a senior data-platform profile.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is plain-text, readable, and likely to parse correctly. It includes useful terms such as Python, TDMS, CSV, SQL Server, staging table, Power BI, reusable tools, automated checks, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, and Git. However, keyword coverage for this specific role is limited because the letter does not naturally mention data quality standards, reusable frameworks, data platform capabilities, data architecture, or open-source practices. It correctly does not claim unsupported technologies such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, or dimensional modelling. AI screening probability is moderate to low for this senior role: the quantified evidence is credible and relevant, but the substantial gaps in cloud, platform-scale operations, advanced SQL, and data modelling will likely reduce matching against the job's core requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's transferable aspects: reusable internal tools, automated data-quality checks against specifications, SQL Server workflows, BI collaboration, ownership of a maintained process, and measurable reduction of unnecessary manual work. These points support Halden Pay's Together, Ownership, and Pace themes. The candidate's material does not demonstrate production data-platform or cloud-warehouse experience at scale, advanced Python and SQL including query optimisation, strong dimensional data modelling, or Google Cloud/comparable cloud experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects in the letter. The document also does not explicitly mention native Portuguese, although the candidate has it. The transition is credible, but the overall alignment is materially below the stated Senior Data Engineer requirements.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. **Critical — remove repetition:** In the third body paragraph, delete the sentence beginning **“My experience so far has focused...”** or merge its useful content into the preceding paragraph. The following two sentences repeat the course and project information already stated: **“I am currently completing an online data engineering course...”** and **“Alongside my professional work, I am completing an online data engineering course...”**. Keep the course detail once, with the accurate wording **“six of nine modules completed.”**

2. **Strengthen role alignment without adding unsupported claims:** In the paragraph describing the Corvane work, revise the final sentence so it uses the advertisement's supported concepts of reusable frameworks, data quality, and internal platform capabilities without calling the work a production data platform. For example: **“These projects gave me practical experience building reusable internal data workflows, enforcing automated data-quality checks against specifications, and delivering outputs that validation and design teams rely on.”**

3. **Make the company-values connection evidence-based:** In the paragraph beginning **“Halden Pay’s focus...”**, replace the broad appeal statement with a sentence tied to the candidate's demonstrated work. For example: **“Halden Pay’s emphasis on Together, Ownership and Pace appeals to me because I have maintained a shared internal tool, supported four test engineers, and reduced a repetitive reporting process from about three days to half a day.”**

4. **Add the supported language qualification:** In the final paragraph before the closing, add a concise sentence such as **“I am a native Portuguese speaker and use English professionally.”** This makes the Portuguese-plus-English requirement visible without overstating language capability.

5. **Improve the closing specificity:** Replace **“I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my test-data automation experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team”** with a version that accurately frames the transition, such as **“I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building reliable engineering-data workflows could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team as I continue developing toward data engineering.”** Do not add cloud, orchestration, data-modelling, or senior platform claims that are not supported by the candidate information.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building reliable engineering-data workflows could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team as I continue developing toward data engineering.

Best regards,
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, concise, and well structured. It uses specific, credible evidence: processing approximately 2 GB of weekly test data, reducing reporting time from three days to half a day, supporting four engineers, and delivering a dashboard used by approximately 15 colleagues. The transition from mechanical engineering into data engineering is explained honestly. However, the letter presents a relatively junior and learning-oriented profile for a Senior Data Engineer role, and it could make the technical scope of the existing work more precise by naming the supported technologies and operational context. The closing is somewhat repetitive and could end more directly.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-readable: it uses standard paragraphs, no problematic graphics or formatting, and includes relevant terms such as Python, SQL Server, Power BI, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git, data-quality checks, and data workflows. It does not include unsupported keywords such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, or CI/CD, which is appropriate. For stronger keyword coverage based on the candidate's actual experience, the main project paragraph could include pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, TDMS/CSV, SQL Server staging table, Windows Task Scheduler, and npTDMS. The document is unlikely to pass a strict senior-level screening because it does not demonstrate the ad's core platform, cloud, advanced SQL, or data-modelling requirements; this is a candidate-background gap rather than an ATS formatting defect.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's emphasis on reusable internal workflows, automated data-quality checks, ownership, collaboration, and reducing unnecessary complexity. The examples support the Together, Ownership, and Pace values: the tool is shared by four engineers, the dashboard serves approximately 15 colleagues, and reporting time was substantially reduced. Portuguese and professional English are shown, and the candidate's interest in developing in data engineering is credible. However, the candidate's material shows substantial gaps against the senior role: no production data platform or cloud data warehouse at scale, no Google Cloud or comparable cloud, no advanced SQL or query optimisation on large datasets, no strong data modelling or dimensional modelling experience, and no hands-on Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, CI/CD, or production container deployment. The letter should not imply equivalence to those requirements. Graph modelling is also not evidenced. The strongest truthful positioning is as an engineer transitioning into data engineering with practical experience in engineering-data automation and internal reporting workflows.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the second paragraph, replace the opening sentence with a more technically specific version that preserves the existing evidence: "At Corvane Automotive Components, I developed Python scripts using pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and npTDMS to parse approximately 2 GB of TDMS and CSV test-rig output each week, validate channels against specifications, and generate standard report figures." This improves ATS coverage without claiming unsupported senior-level Python expertise.

2. In the second paragraph, clarify the operational scope of the internal workflow instead of describing it generally as a "reusable internal data workflow": "I also maintain this internal tool as a nightly Windows Task Scheduler job on a laboratory PC; it writes summary results to a SQL Server staging table created by IT and is used by four other test engineers." This accurately demonstrates operation and reuse while avoiding any implication that it is a cloud production platform.

3. In the third paragraph, make the learning project evidence more concrete and truthful by changing "I am building a small Python project with Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, and Git" to "Alongside my professional work, I maintain a small personal Flask API using SQLite, Docker Compose and Git; it runs locally and was built as part of my data-engineering learning." This gives context for the limited scope and avoids overstating deployment experience.

4. In the final paragraph, remove the repeated statement about "continue developing" and use a more direct close tied to the strongest evidence: "I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience with Python-based test-data automation, SQL Server reporting workflows, automated data-quality checks and cross-team engineering tools could contribute to Halden Pay's Data Platform team." Keep the existing statement about professional English and Portuguese, but avoid presenting the candidate as already meeting the senior platform requirements.
